newsitem.title: TURKEY: Demirel asks EU not to forget Turkey at summit.
newsitem.headline: Demirel asks EU not to forget Turkey at summit.

text.p: Turkish President Suleyman Demirel has written to the 15 leaders of European Union countries to ask them not to forget Turkey's bid for full membership when they meet at the Dublin summit, an aide said on Thursday.

"The EU will talk about its future enlargement at the Dublin summit. The president sent letters to remind the leaders Turkey has a privileged position for full membership of the union, because it is a stable, secular and democratic country," the adviser told Reuters.
EU leaders will meet for two days in Dublin from Friday to discuss the single currency, enlargement into eastern Europe, fighting drugs and the future of EU institutions.
Turkey's Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan has turned down an invitation to dine with EU ministers during the summit, saying he did so to warn Europe about its coolness towards Turkey.
Europe has put Turkey's application for EU membership on hold because of Ankara's economic troubles, human rights record and disputes with member Greece.
Turkish officials bemoan the fact that former communist nations of eastern Europe have streaked ahead of it in the queue for full membership.
